3 · ACOLITE PROCESSING PROGRESS

Two pilot scenes processed and evaluated

For each pilot scene, the same L1C image was processed twice. The first result used ACOLITE atmospheric correction only. The second used the same atmospheric correction followed by sunglint correction. Comparing these two results shows the effect of the sunglint step before batch processing begins.

Pilot processing complete
Scene 1: Fiji test scene17 January 2026 · tile T60KXD · independent L1C scene from the Fiji download folder.
Scene 2: supplied glinted scene29 October 2025 · tile T60KXE · the ZIP identified visually as containing strong glint.
How Rrs is known before sunglint correction: “before” is not the raw Sentinel‑2 L1C measurement. ACOLITE first performs DSF atmospheric correction and outputs surface reflectance (ρs). The control run keeps sunglint correction off, and its Rrs is Rrsbefore = ρsDSF only / π. The paired corrected run gives Rrsafter = ρsDSF + glint / π.
RESULT

Visual glint patterns and numerical glint values decreased

ACOLITE calculates a glint indicator from the short-wave infrared (SWIR) bands, where the water-leaving signal from clear water is normally very low. If visible Rrs still follows the same spatial pattern, residual glint is present. The before/after test found a lower relationship in both pilot scenes, while blue/green Rrs remained mostly positive.

Interpretation: masked blue and green Rrs from these two scenes passed the internal glint and negative-value checks used in this report. This is evidence of correction performance, not proof of absolute Rrs accuracy; no matching field-radiometer measurement was available.

Rrs use

  • Blue and green: use after cloud, land and bad-pixel masks.
  • Red: use carefully over shallow or turbid water.
  • Red-edge and NIR: mainly for masks and quality checks.
  • Cloud, whitecap and saturated-glint pixels: remove.
1 · Visual evaluation

The broad bright-grey glint pattern over the ocean became darker and more uniform after correction. Clouds, land and reef features remained visible and must be masked separately.

2 · Numerical glint evaluation

Mean glint correlation decreased from 0.373 to 0.066 in Scene 1 and from 0.317 to 0.154 in Scene 2. Lower values indicate less remaining glint.

3 · Rrs quality evaluation

Invalid negative blue/green pixels remained below 0.21%, well below the 5% scene-screening limit used in this assessment.

Processing note: the L1C cards are ACOLITE inputs. L2A cards are included to document the downloaded collection and are retained for comparison or other analyses.

METHOD

What ACOLITE does and how the scenes were processed

ACOLITE is software developed for satellite observations of coastal and inland water. It converts Sentinel‑2 L1C data into water reflectance by removing atmospheric effects. An additional correction estimates and removes sunlight reflected directly from the water surface.

01 · INPUT

Sentinel‑2 L1C

Top-of-atmosphere satellite reflectance and sun/view geometry were read from each scene.

02 · ATMOSPHERE

DSF correction

Dark Spectrum Fitting estimated aerosol effects and removed atmospheric scattering from the image.

03 · SUNGLINT

SWIR-based correction

The SWIR bands were used to estimate surface glare, which was then removed from the visible bands.

04 · OUTPUT

Rrs and quality flags

ACOLITE produced Rrs bands and flags for clouds, land, invalid values and other unsuitable pixels.

ACOLITE correction concept

DSF · ATMOSPHERE

1. Find the atmospheric contribution

Sentinel‑2 L1C measures light at the top of the atmosphere. ACOLITE first corrects gaseous absorption and Rayleigh scattering. Dark Spectrum Fitting then searches for the darkest suitable pixels across the scene and bands. Their remaining signal is used to fit the aerosol path reflectance.

ρTOA ≈ atmosphere + transmitted surface signal
DSF · OUTPUT

2. Recover surface reflectance

The fitted atmospheric contribution is removed band by band and atmospheric transmission is accounted for. The result is surface reflectance (ρs). The DSF-only control run stops here, so it provides the Rrs used as “before glint correction.”

Rrs_before(λ) = ρs_DSF-only(λ) / π
SUNGLINT · REFERENCE

3. Estimate the glint pattern from SWIR

Over clear deep water, water-leaving reflectance in the short-wave infrared is normally very low. Spatial SWIR surface-reflectance remaining after DSF is therefore used as a reference image for surface glare. Cloud, land and unsuitable pixels are excluded.

glint reference ≈ residual SWIR surface signal
SUNGLINT · CORRECTION

4. Remove the estimated surface glare

ACOLITE transfers the SWIR glint estimate to each visible/NIR band with a band-dependent factor and subtracts it. The corrected surface reflectance is then converted to Rrs. The before and after tests use the same scene and DSF settings.

ρs_after(λ) = ρs_before(λ) − scaled glint reference

What this correction does not do: it does not remove clouds, repair saturated pixels or reconstruct information lost under extremely strong glare. These pixels remain masked.

Rrs before sunglint correctionRrs_before(λ) = ρs_DSF-only(λ) / π

This value comes from the paired ACOLITE control run. Atmospheric correction has already been completed, but sunglint removal is off.

Rrs after sunglint correctionRrs_after(λ) = ρs_DSF+glint(λ) / π

This value comes from the same L1C scene and DSF settings with sunglint removal on. Both Rrs quantities have unit sr⁻¹.

Glint-correlation test|r(λ)| = |correlation[Rrs(λ), glint reference]|

|r| ranges from 0 to 1. Lower values after correction mean that the Rrs image follows the glint pattern less strongly.

Reported glint reduction100 × (1 − |r after| / |r before|)

A positive percentage means the relationship with glint decreased. The scene summary uses the mean |r| of Coastal blue, Blue, Green and Red.

Invalid negative-pixel percentage100 × count(Rrs < 0) / valid water pixels

Rrs below zero is not physically valid. A small percentage indicates that correction did not create widespread invalid water values.

Normalized reference comparisonnormalized Rrs(λ) = Rrs(λ) / maximum Rrs

Only the separate reference graph scales each spectrum to 1.0. It compares the wavelength pattern with NOAA MOBY and the HydroLight simulation; it does not establish absolute accuracy.

Comparison pixelsone common mask for before and after

Correlation and negative-value checks use the same valid-water pixels after flags. Median spectra use the same conservative low-red/NIR water subset. Land, cirrus, very bright pixels and pixels outside the image are excluded.

Meaning of Rrs: remote-sensing reflectance (Rrs, sr⁻¹) describes the light leaving the water relative to the sunlight reaching it. The “before” Rrs is obtained from the DSF-only ACOLITE output, not from raw L1C. The “after” Rrs adds only the sunglint correction. The SWIR correction approach follows Harmel et al., Remote Sensing of Environment.

MATCHED WATER ZOOM

Visual check of the same open-water area

Both panels use the same location, zoom and display scaling. Compare the grey water background and diagonal glint texture—not the white clouds.

Visual interpretation: disappearance of a bright water pattern supports successful glint removal, but the numerical |r| decrease is used with the image because display brightness alone is not a quantitative validation.

Keterangan: what values are used in the graphs?

Rrs graph

Yes—the dots are median values from many water pixels. For each Sentinel‑2 band, one median Rrs in sr⁻¹ is calculated from the same clear-water candidate pixels. The smooth line only connects the band medians; it is not the spectrum of one pixel.

Glint graph

The plotted value is the absolute Pearson correlation |r| between pixel-by-pixel Rrs and ACOLITE’s SWIR-derived glint-reference image, using the same valid water pixels. A lower value after correction means less of the glint pattern remains.

Reference-spectrum graph

The grey and teal curves show the before and after spectra. Each spectrum is scaled to a maximum of 1.0 so its wavelength pattern can be compared with NOAA MOBY and the numerical HydroLight Rrs simulation. It is not an absolute-accuracy test.

How were the water pixels selected?

1Sample the scene

The 20 m output grid was sampled every fifth row and fifth column—one of every 25 pixels, with 100 m spacing in each direction.

2Remove unsuitable pixels

ACOLITE flags removed non-water, cirrus, very bright/high-TOA, outside-scene and mixed pixels. Pixels also had to contain finite before and after values in every evaluated band.

3Select the spectral-test subset

One shared low-red/NIR mask was defined from corrected Rrs: Green > 0; Red from 0 to <0.006 sr⁻¹; and NIR from −0.001 to <0.004 sr⁻¹. The identical mask was then applied to both before and after spectra.

4Apply each test

The median-Rrs line uses the low-red/NIR subset. Glint correlation and negative-pixel percentages use all valid sampled water pixels.

This scene: 816,254 valid sampled water pixels were evaluated; 690,716 pixels (84.6%) met the low-red/NIR criteria used for the median spectral lines.

Numerical values plotted in the graphs

The Rrs columns are the median values plotted in the first graph. The correlation column contains the |r| values plotted in the second graph. The same comparison masks are used for the before and after values.

PRODUCTION-SCALE IMPLEMENTATION

Proposed quality-controlled processing workflow

The two-scene results support further processing subject to consistent scene-level acceptance criteria and documented quality control.

Prerequisites identified
  1. Verify the completed download set. Match each selected product, validate SAFE/ZIP structure and checksum where available; process L1C with ACOLITE. Retain L2A as comparison or contextual data rather than ACOLITE input.
  2. Pre-screen geometry and contamination. Record sun/view/glint angle, cloud fraction, land adjacency, whitecaps and saturation. Apply residual-glint correction where geometry or image diagnostics indicate contamination risk.
  3. Run reproducibly. Pin the ACOLITE code version and settings; retain per-scene logs, L2R, L2W/Rrs, RGB previews and QA summaries. Resolve ancillary-data access before production processing or document the applied defaults.
  4. Apply consistent acceptance criteria. Mean visible-band |r| with the glint reference should decrease; corrected blue/green negative-pixel frequency should remain below 5%; clear-water red/NIR should remain low; and image previews should show no correction-induced seams or striping.
  5. Classify outputs. Assign PASS for blue/green analysis, CONDITIONAL for red or benthic applications, and FAIL/REPROCESS for cloud contamination, saturated glint, widespread negative Rrs or persistent glint structure. Preserve quality masks with each product.
  6. Conduct external validation when field data become available. Match ACOLITE Rrs with radiometer Rrs and report per-band bias, RMSE, mean absolute percentage error and correlation following NASA SeaBASS matchup procedures.

Study limitations

  • No coincident field radiometer was available; therefore, satellite Rrs could not be tested against a same-place, same-time field measurement.
  • The NOAA MOBY spectrum is rescaled only in the separate normalized-comparison graph. It is not treated as a Fiji accuracy reference because the location and date differ.
  • The HydroLight spectrum is a numerical model result, not a same-place, same-time field measurement. Band-centre interpolation is used here; full sensor response-function convolution remains a future refinement.
  • Water spectra vary with bottom depth, coloured dissolved material, phytoplankton and suspended sediment.
  • Ancillary meteorology retrieval failed for both scene runs; ACOLITE applied defaults of ozone 0.30, water vapor 1.50 and pressure 1013.25.
  • Strong or saturated sunglint represents information loss that cannot be reconstructed through correction.
Paper and data sources. Software: official ACOLITE repository. DSF atmospheric correction: Vanhellemont & Ruddick. SWIR sunglint method: Harmel et al.. Field-radiometry method: NASA MOBY/SeaBASS. Clear-ocean reference data: NOAA MOBY M276, 28 March 2024. HydroLight numerical simulation. HydroLight model information: HydroLight/EcoLight User’s Guide. Matchup guidance: NASA SeaBASS.
Generated from ACOLITE NetCDF outputs, QA metrics, the cited NOAA field spectrum and 101 numerical HydroLight Rrs simulation values. The reference spectra are normalized only in the comparison panel; no coincident field validation is claimed.
